description: Hand-reviewed decisions for canonical_threat_actors.json. scripts/build_canonical_threat_actors.py applies them after the galaxy rules, so a rebuild never drops them: 'never_merge' with an 'actor' first takes the names away from that actor and never gives them back to it; 'merge' makes each name a synonym of the actor with the canonical key 'into' (an actor without an ATT&CK id that a name is the key of is folded into it; a key that no actor has yet creates the actor); 'never_merge' without an 'actor' takes each name out of every actor and lists it under 'ambiguous'; 'canonical_name' sets the display name of the actor with the key 'key' (a name with another key re-keys the actor and keeps the old key as a synonym). Where two graph nodes are spelling variants of one name, the canonical is the node with more relationships, so that fewer edges move, unless it is an ATT&CK group's name. Each decision states its reason, date and status: 'proposed' until reviewed, then 'accepted'. Both are applied.

merge.reason: MITRE uses Lazarus Group (G0032) as an umbrella name, and the bare name is used the same way. On the graph the two nodes share seven malware families (BeaverTail, BLINDINGCAN, FudModule, InvisibleFerret, LightlessCan, Manuscrypt, ThreatNeedle); the galaxy also lists Lazarus as a synonym of this group.
Short form of the ATT&CK name of G0034; the threat-actor and ICS galaxies name this group Sandworm. On the graph the two nodes share Cyclops Blink, Industroyer2 and Prestige.
Short form of the ATT&CK name of G0047, also a galaxy synonym of this group. On the graph the two nodes share GammaLoad, GammaSteel and Pteranodon.

The ATT&CK name of G0138 with ' group' appended. The node's report describes Andariel's SmallTiger and ModeLoader campaign; no malware is shared with the ATT&CK node, whose links come from ATT&CK only.

Kept: Lotus Panda is a widely used name of Lotus Blossom (G0030). The threat-actor galaxy links its Lotus Panda record to G0030, and on the graph the two nodes share Chrysalis, Cobalt Strike and Sagerunex (46 and 64 relationships).
Name variant of the Interlock ransomware gang (an OTX-only actor, not in the galaxy). Both nodes carry the Interlock ransomware family and both reports describe the gang.
Name variant of the Beast ransomware-as-a-service gang (an OTX-only actor). Both nodes carry the Monster family, Beast's predecessor, and both reports describe the gang.

Name variant of the Fog ransomware gang (an OTX-only actor). Both nodes carry the Fog ransomware family; the group node's report is about a Fog affiliate's tooling. The bare word 'fog' is too common to be the key.

The same distinctive name with the descriptor 'APT' (an OTX-only actor). Both reports describe the ForumTroll group's targeted attacks on organisations in Russia, one the original operation and one a later phishing campaign. No malware or pulse is shared, and no other actor uses the name.

Silver Fox is its own canonical actor (see the never_merge with Void Arachne). 'silver fox apt' (29 relationships) adds the descriptor 'APT', 'silverfox' (69) drops the space; 'silver fox' (25) shares ValleyRAT with both and ABCDoor and RustSL with 'silverfox'. 'silverfox' holds the most relationships, but the canonical keeps the name as written in the galaxy and the reports.

Spacing variant of the ATT&CK name of G0082. The threat-actor galaxy files APT38 under Lazarus Group, so without this decision 'apt 38' would be a Lazarus Group synonym, while ATT&CK keeps APT38 a group of its own (the bare 'apt38' already stays with G0082).
Konni with ' group' appended; the galaxy lists Konni as a synonym of Opal Sleet, and the node shares EndRAT, RemcosRAT and RftRAT with the 'opal sleet' node.
Spelling variant of the Black Basta ransomware gang (OTX-only). 'black basta' holds 42 relationships, 'blackbasta' 41; they share the Black Basta, Cobalt Strike, DarkGate and SystemBC families.
Spelling variant of the Clop ransomware gang (OTX-only). 'clop' holds 93 relationships, 'cl0p' 68; both reports describe the gang's file-transfer exploitation campaigns and they share LemurLoot.
Spelling variant of the Dire Wolf ransomware gang that emerged in May 2025 (OTX-only). 'direwolf' holds 18 relationships, 'dire wolf' 10; both carry the Dire Wolf ransomware family.

Spelling variant of ATT&CK's Transparent Tribe (G0134; 62 relationships against 24). The node's report describes a Pakistan-nexus espionage campaign against Indian military targets, which is Transparent Tribe's.
Spelling variant of ATT&CK's TeamPCP (G1056; 151 relationships against 3). Both report supply-chain attacks on package registries, and they share router_runtime.js.
Spelling variant of ATT&CK's CyberAv3ngers (G1027; 61 relationships against 25); the galaxy's 'Cyber Av3ngers' record joins the ATT&CK group by its spacing, and the two nodes share IOCONTROL.

Spelling variant of Blind Eagle, which the galaxy lists as a synonym of APT-C-36 (G0099). On the graph of 2026-10-16 the 'blindeagle' node (38 relationships) shares Caminho, DCRat and Remcos RAT with the ATT&CK node.

ATT&CK lists Callisto Group as an alias of Star Blizzard (G1033); the galaxy keeps Callisto as a cluster of its own, whose synonyms (TAG-53, UNC4057, Blue Callisto) name the same COLDRIVER activity. On the graph of 2026-10-16 the 'callisto' node carries LOSTKEYS, NOROBOT, YESROBOT, MAYBEROBOT and COLDCOPY, which public reporting attributes to COLDRIVER / Star Blizzard.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary; the threat-actor galaxy lists no group under this name. The decision reads a shared codebase and a note naming the cartel as a brand within the DragonForce cartel, so DEVMAN is an actor of its own. A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary; the threat-actor galaxy lists no group under this name. The ransomware galaxy lists HelloKitty (since November 2020, synonym FiveHands); malpedia lists it for Windows and ELF and ATT&CK as HELLOKITTY (S0617). The threat-actor galaxy describes UNC2447, an actor the reference holds, as a financially motivated actor with ties to multiple hacker groups, 'observed deploying ransomware, including FiveHands and Hello Kitty'; ATT&CK and malpedia list FIVEHANDS and HELLOKITTY as separate software. The galaxies describe UNC2447 as deploying ransomware, not as HelloKitty's developer or operator, so the operation is an actor of its own; a merge into 'unc2447' is the alternative decision. A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary; the threat-actor galaxy lists no group under this name. INC Ransom is an actor the reference holds. A bought codebase does not name Lynx's operator, so the operation is an actor of its own; a merge into 'inc ransom' is the alternative decision. The threat actors whose names contain the word (Hidden Lynx, Silent Lynx, Cosmic Lynx) are other actors. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node (21 relationships) carries the Lynx family.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary; the threat-actor galaxy lists no group under this name. The ransomware galaxy lists 'vect'; ATT&CK describes TeamPCP (G1056) as partnering with ransomware actors including Vect, a partnership, not an attribution. A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary; the threat-actor galaxy lists no group under this name. A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary; the threat-actor galaxy lists no group under this name. The ransomware galaxy lists 'yurei'. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node (24 relationships) carries the Yurei family.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary. The ransomware galaxy says Conti was developed by the TrickBot group, the threat-actor galaxy describes Wizard Spider as the operator of the TrickBot malware, malpedia says Conti is thought to be led by the group known as Wizard Spider, and ATT&CK records that Wizard Spider (G0102) uses Conti (S0575); the reference already holds GOLD ULRICK, a name for Conti's operators, as a synonym of Wizard Spider. The name therefore counts as Wizard Spider, and the actor alias merge folds an OTX actor node 'Conti' into the Wizard Spider node. The reference keeps Storm-0230 ('Conti Team 1', whose record lists WIZARD SPIDER as a synonym) as an actor of its own, so 'Conti Team 1' does not resolve to Wizard Spider. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node (27 relationships) carries Conti, Ryuk and TrickBot.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary. The threat-actor galaxy records that BITWISE SPIDER uses LockBit (estimated as likely) and that BITWISE SPIDER's leak site has posted the most victims each month since July 2021 through LockBit 2.0; the other actors the galaxies link to LockBit deploy or use it, and no galaxy names another developer or operator. The name therefore counts as BITWISE SPIDER; the actor alias merge folds an OTX actor node 'LockBit' into a BITWISE SPIDER node when the graph holds one, and otherwise the node keeps its name. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node had 71 relationships.

A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: an OTX report names it as the adversary. The threat-actor galaxy describes GOLD MANSARD as the group that operated the Nemty ransomware, whose operator retired Nemty in April 2020, after which Nefilim was introduced without an affiliate model; the ransomware galaxy relates Nefilim to Nemty and lists Nefilim among the later names of JSWorm, the family that became Nemty. The threat-actor galaxy names TRAVELING SPIDER, an actor the reference holds, as the developer of Nemty; it does not name Nefilim. The name therefore counts as GOLD MANSARD; the actor alias merge folds an OTX actor node 'Nefilim' into a GOLD MANSARD node when the graph holds one, and otherwise the node keeps its name. On the graph of 2026-10-17 the node had 14 relationships.

Spelling variant of SAMBASPIDER, which the threat-actor galaxy lists as the actor associated with the Mispadu banking trojan. The OTX report on the graph's 'samba spider' node names the adversary 'SAMBA SPIDER' and reviews the Latin American banking malware of 2024, Mispadu among it. No galaxy gives either spelling to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 28 relationships, among them Mispadu; the graph holds no 'sambaspider' node.

Spelling variant of Markopolo, which the threat-actor galaxy describes as an actor that runs scams against cryptocurrency users through a fake application, Vortax, and uses social media to make them look legitimate. The OTX report on the graph's 'marko polo' node names the adversary 'Marko Polo', a cybercriminal group that runs scams through social media, impersonating brands of virtual-meeting and cryptocurrency software, with Stealc, Rhadamanthys and HijackLoader. No galaxy gives either spelling to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 16 relationships; the graph holds no 'markopolo' node.

Spelling variant of TA558, which the threat-actor galaxy describes as a financially motivated actor that sends malicious e-mails with business-themed lures to distribute at least 15 different malware payloads. The OTX report on the graph's 'ta-558' node names the adversary 'TA-558' for a spearphishing campaign that delivers Snake Keylogger. No galaxy gives either spelling to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 10 relationships; the graph holds no 'ta558' node.

Spelling variant of 'isoon', which the microsoft-activity-group and threat-actor galaxies list as a synonym of Houndstooth Typhoon. The OTX report on the graph's 'i-soon' node names the adversary 'I-SOON', the Chinese contractor whose leaked documents tie it to several state-sponsored groups. No galaxy gives the name to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 11 relationships, ten of them techniques, and no malware; the graph holds no 'houndstooth typhoon' node.

APT-C-13 is the 360net-threat-actor galaxy's designation of Sandworm. Its record, the Chinese name of Sandworm with the designation (synonym SandWorm), is the only galaxy record that carries the designation, and the galaxy relates it to the threat-actor galaxy's Sandworm record and the microsoft-activity-group galaxy's Seashell Blizzard record, both joined to Sandworm Team (G0034). The build leaves the record out because its name without the designation joins no ATT&CK actor. Both OTX reports on the graph's 'apt-c-13' node state that APT-C-13 (Sandworm) is also known as FROZENBARENTS, an ATT&CK alias of G0034, and one names the adversary 'APT-C-13, Sandworm, FROZENBARENTS'. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 28 relationships, 26 of them techniques, and no malware.

APT-C-53 is the 360net-threat-actor galaxy's designation of Gamaredon. Its record 'Gamaredon - APT-C-53' is the only galaxy record that carries the designation. It describes a Russian state-sponsored group, active since at least 2013, that targets Ukrainian government, defence, diplomatic and media organisations, and it names Primitive Bear, Winterflounder and BlueAlpha, which the reference holds as synonyms of Gamaredon Group (G0047). The build leaves the record out because its name without the designation joins no ATT&CK actor. Both OTX reports on the graph's 'apt-c-53' node name the adversary 'APT-C-53 (Gamaredon)': one states that APT-C-53 is also known as Gamaredon, the other that it is also known as Primitive Bear, Winterflounder and BlueAlpha. No galaxy gives the designation to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node has 22 relationships, 21 of them techniques, and no malware.

APT-C-55 is the 360net-threat-actor galaxy's designation of Kimsuky. Its record 'Kimsuky - APT-C-55' is the only galaxy record that carries the designation. It describes a North Korean group, first reported in 2013, that targets South Korean think tanks and government, diplomatic, media and academic organisations. The build joins the record to Kimsuky (G0094), whose synonyms include 'kimsuky - apt-c-55'. The OTX report on the graph's 'apt-c-55' node names the adversary 'APT-C-55 (Kimsuky)'. It describes a campaign against South Korea with the HappyDoor backdoor whose scripts, backdoor families and domain naming match Kimsuky's earlier activity. No galaxy gives the designation to another actor. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the node (19 relationships, one OTX report) carries HappyDoor, which another OTX report attributes to the Kimsuky node.

An OTX report names the adversary 'TA4557/FIN6', which the actor-name hygiene keeps as one name because it does not split on '/'. The report covers an intrusion that began with a resume lure and used More_eggs, Cobalt Strike, Pyramid C2 and Cloudflared. Both parts of the name belong to FIN6 (G0037): FIN6 is its ATT&CK name, and the threat-actor galaxy lists TA4557 among FIN6's synonyms (the reference holds 'ta4557' as a synonym of FIN6). No galaxy gives either name to another actor. The three OTX reports on the FIN6 node describe the same activity: two report resume and job-seeker lures delivering More_eggs, one reports Pyramid C2 servers, and all three list More_eggs, Terra Loader, SKID and SpicyOmelette. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the 'ta4557/fin6' node (32 relationships, one OTX report) shares More_eggs and Terra Loader with the FIN6 node.

Replaces the merge of 'agenda' into an actor 'qilin' of 2026-10-17. A ransomware operation named after its ransomware: OTX reports name Qilin and Agenda as the adversary. ATT&CK describes Water Galura (G1050) as the operators of the Qilin Ransomware-as-a-Service, who handle payload generation, ransom negotiations and the publication of stolen data. ATT&CK also lists Agenda as an alias of Qilin (S1242), and malpedia records that Qilin was first observed in July 2022 under the name Agenda, so Agenda is Qilin's earlier name. ATT&CK and malpedia describe Qilin as run with affiliates. The only other group ATT&CK links to it, Moonstone Sleet (G1036), uses it, and no galaxy names another developer or operator. The names therefore count as Water Galura, and the actor alias merge folds OTX actor nodes 'Qilin' and 'Agenda' into the Water Galura node. On the graph of 2026-10-22 the 'qilin' node (84 relationships, eight OTX reports, 'agenda' already folded into it) carries the Qilin and Agenda families, and the Water Galura node uses Qilin.

never_merge.reason: Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy lists Silver Fox as a synonym of Void Arachne, a vendor equivalence that is not universally accepted (the two share ValleyRAT and Winos 4.0, families several Chinese-speaking clusters use). A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy lists Famous Chollima as a synonym of Wagemole, a vendor equivalence that is not universally accepted (both name overlapping North Korean IT-worker and fake-interview activity). A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy lists TA488 as a synonym of Void Blizzard, a vendor equivalence that is not universally accepted; the two graph nodes share no malware or pulse. A wrong merge is worse than a missed one.

Doubtful: the node's only malware link is 'green lambert - s0690', an unrelated ATT&CK malware family that looks like a bad extraction (the name appears inside 'Lambert'); merging would carry that link to the gang. Its report and that of 'bert ransomware' describe the same gang, so revisit once the extraction is fixed.

Doubtful: the node's only report is a monthly vulnerability-prioritisation digest, not an Interlock report, and none of its malware links (GhostBlade, GhostKnife, GhostSaber, PlasmaGrid, PlasmaLoader) is shared with the other Interlock nodes; merging would attach them to the gang.

A malware family name, not a group. A galaxy lists it as a synonym of Storm-2460, but an actor node named after the stealer gathers reports on its many distributors; merging would attribute all of them to one group.

Common words that only the suffix rule derives, from 'Comment Group' (APT1), 'Tsar Team' (APT28), 'Beijing Group' (Elderwood), 'Iron Group' and 'Hacking Team'. As bare names they do not identify one actor.

Doubtful short forms the suffix rule derives from 'Tonto Team' (G0131) and 'Pacha Group': both are common words (Spanish 'tonto', and a title and brand name), and the reports name the groups in full. Neither is a graph name today. The other short forms checked (gorgon, sunshop, chronus, belsen, daixin) are distinctive and kept.

A malware family name. ATT&CK lists 'BlackEnergy (Group)' as an alias of Sandworm Team (G0034); EdgeGuard's actor-name hygiene drops the parenthetical, which leaves the malware's name, so the bare name is not taken as the group ('blackenergy group' still is).

Bare names that only the suffix rule derives, from 'Poseidon Group' (G0033) and 'Shamoon Group'; both are also malware family names (the Poseidon stealer, the Shamoon wiper used by several groups), so the bare name does not identify one actor.

Not merged: the threat-actor galaxy's record 'Cold River' (synonyms Nahr Elbard and Nahr el bared) has one reference, a report on the Agent_Drable implant, which malpedia lists as a synonym of the DNSpionage malware. The record describes an actor that uses DNS subdomain hijacking, certificate spoofing and tunnelled command-and-control traffic, and it has no galaxy relation to Star Blizzard (G1033) or to the threat-actor galaxy's Callisto record. The build joins it to Star Blizzard only because 'Cold River' is a spacing variant of COLDRIVER, an ATT&CK alias of G1033. No Star Blizzard or Callisto record in any galaxy lists the three names. The names are kept away from Star Blizzard and resolve to no actor. The decision takes the names, not the join: the record stays listed among Star Blizzard's records and gives it none of its names.
